claims.quote: 'Snowstorm' uterus, no fetal parts, theca-lutein cysts, very high β-hCG Hydatidiform mole

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Suggestive ultrasound findings when evaluating a pregnancy: eg, a mass containing multiple cysts, absence of a fetus and amniotic fluid
claims.quote: Suggestive findings (eg, mass containing multiple cysts, absence of a fetus and amniotic fluid) seen during ultrasonography done to evaluate pregnancy

claims.text: Suspected with a positive pregnancy test plus any of: unexpectedly high beta-hCG (except placental site and epithelioid trophoblastic tumors, which give low levels), uterus much larger than expected for dates, preeclampsia in the 1st or 2nd trimester, vaginal passage of grapelike tissue, suggestive ultrasound findings, unexplained metastases with an unknown primary
claims.quote: Gestational trophoblastic disease is suspected in women with a positive pregnancy test and any of the following: Unexpectedly high levels of beta-hCG detected during pregnancy testing (except for placental site trophoblastic tumor and epithelioid trophoblastic tumor, which result in low beta-hCG levels) Uterine size much larger than expected for dates Symptoms or signs of preeclampsia in 1st or 2nd trimester Vaginal passage of grapelike tissue Suggestive findings (eg, mass containing multiple cysts, absence of a fetus and amniotic fluid) seen during ultrasonography done to evaluate pregnancy Unexplained metastases in women of child-bearing age with an unknown primary tumor

claims.text: Very high beta-hCG and classic ultrasound findings may suggest it, but the diagnosis must be confirmed histologically (evacuated uterine contents or endometrial biopsy)
claims.quote: If gestational trophoblastic disease is suspected, testing includes measurement of serum beta-hCG and, if not previously done, pelvic ultrasonography. Findings (eg, very high beta-hCG levels, classic ultrasonographic findings) may suggest the diagnosis, but the diagnosis must be histologically confirmed through pathology evaluation of evacuated uterine contents or endometrial biopsy.

claims.text: Do ultrasound in early pregnancy if the uterus is much larger than expected for dates, beta-hCG is unexpectedly high, or there are signs of preeclampsia
claims.quote: Do ultrasonography during early pregnancy if uterine size is much larger than expected for dates, if beta-hCG levels are unexpectedly high, or if women have symptoms or signs of preeclampsia.

claims.text: Thyroid function tests if beta-hCG is > 100,000 mIU/mL, to check for hyperthyroidism
claims.quote: Thyroid function tests are done if the beta-hCG level is > 100,000 mIU/mL (> 100,000 IU/L) to check for hyperthyroidism.

claims.text: Causes Hydatidiform moles are benign placental tumors with malignant potential, made of proliferating villous trophoblasts; classified as complete or partial
claims.quote: Hydatiform moles are benign placental tumors with malignant potential. They consist of proliferations of villous trophoblasts. They are further classified as complete or partial moles.

claims.text: Complete mole: abnormal placental tissue and no fetal tissue; diploid, most 46XX from a single sperm that duplicates (ovum nucleus absent or inactivated). Partial mole: may contain normal plus abnormal placental tissue; a fetus may develop but cannot survive; triploid (two sperm or a diploid sperm)
claims.quote: Complete mole: The placental tissue is abnormal, and fetal tissue does not form. Complete moles are diploid. Most are 46XX and result from fertilization by a single sperm that then duplicates; the ovum nucleus is either absent or inactivated. However, some result from dispermic fertilization and can be 46 XY. Partial mole: A partial molar pregnancy may contain normal placental tissue with abnormal placental tissue. A fetus may develop but is not able to survive; miscarriage usually occurs early in the pregnancy. Partial moles are triploid, resulting from fertilization by two sperm or a diploid sperm.

claims.text: Most common in women < 17 or > 35 years and after prior gestational trophoblastic disease; in the US, 1 of 1000 to 1200 pregnancies; usually diagnosed in the first half of pregnancy
claims.quote: Hydatidiform moles are most common among women < 17 or > 35 years old and those who have previously had gestational trophoblastic disease. In the United States, hydatiform moles occur in 1 of 1000 to 1200 pregnancies and in 1 of 600 induced abortions (1, 2). They are usually diagnosed during the first half of pregnancy.

claims.text: Most (> 80%) are benign; choriocarcinoma develops after 2 to 3%, more commonly after a complete mole; after a complete mole, approximately 15 to 20% are treated for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
claims.quote: Most (> 80%) hydatidiform moles are benign. In patients with a prior partial or complete mole, incidence of a second mole in subsequent pregnancies is 1 to 2%. Patients who have had a mole require ultrasonography early in subsequent pregnancies, and the placenta should be sent for pathology evaluation. Patients with consecutive molar pregnancies require germline genetic testing for mutations in NLRP7 and KHDC3L. Choriocarcinoma develops after 2 to 3% of hydatidiform moles, more commonly after a complete than a partial mole. After a complete hydatidiform mole, approximately 15 to 20% of patients are treated for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.

claims.text: Symptoms Starts like early pregnancy, but the uterus often becomes larger than expected within 10 to 16 weeks; commonly vaginal bleeding and severe nausea and vomiting (hyperemesis gravidarum), with no fetal movement or heart sounds; vaginal passage of grapelike tissue strongly suggests it
claims.quote: Initial manifestations of a hydatidiform mole suggest early pregnancy, but the uterus often becomes larger than expected within 10 to 16 weeks gestation. Commonly, women test positive for pregnancy and have vaginal bleeding and severe nausea and vomiting (hyperemesis gravidarum) and fetal movement and fetal heart sounds are absent. Vaginal passage of grapelike tissue strongly suggests the diagnosis.

claims.text: Complications may include severe bleeding (possible hemorrhagic shock), preeclampsia and ovarian theca lutein cysts; less commonly uterine infection and sepsis
claims.quote: Complications, such as the following, may occur: Severe bleeding, with possible hemorrhagic shock Preeclampsia Ovarian theca lutein cysts Less common complications include uterine infection and sepsis.

claims.text: Hyperthyroidism is more common (tachycardia, warm skin, sweating, heat intolerance, mild tremors)
claims.quote: Hyperthyroidism is more common among women with gestational trophoblastic disease than in those without. Symptoms can include tachycardia, warm skin, sweating, heat intolerance, and mild tremors.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: D&C; serial β-hCG monitoring
claims.locator: Non-Trauma Ultrasound Findings, OB / Pelvic table

claims.text: Hydatidiform mole is evacuated by suction curettage; alternatively, hysterectomy if childbearing is not planned
claims.quote: Hydatidiform mole, invasive mole, placental site trophoblastic tumor, and epithelioid trophoblastic tumor are evacuated by suction curettage. Alternatively, if childbearing is not planned, hysterectomy may be done.

claims.text: Afterward: chest x-ray; serial serum beta-hCG, with effective contraception while it is monitored; not normalized within 10 weeks = persistent disease → CT of the brain, chest, abdomen and pelvis
claims.quote: A chest x-ray is taken. Serum beta-hCG is measured serially. Effective contraception is recommended while hCG is being monitored. If the beta-hCG level does not normalize within 10 weeks, the disease is classified as persistent. Persistent disease requires CT of the brain, chest, abdomen, and pelvis. Results dictate whether disease is classified as nonmetastatic or metastatic.

claims.text: Persistent disease is usually treated with chemotherapy; success = at least 3 consecutive normal weekly serum beta-hCG levels; prevent pregnancy for 6 months after treatment
claims.quote: Persistent disease is usually treated with chemotherapy. Treatment is considered successful if at least 3 consecutive serum beta-hCG measurements at 1-week intervals are normal. Pregnancy should be prevented for 6 months after treatment because pregnancy would increase beta-hCG levels, making it difficult to determine whether treatment has been successful.

claims.text: Usually any type can be successfully diagnosed and treated, and fertility can be preserved
claims.quote: Usually, any type of gestational trophoblastic disease can be successfully diagnosed and treated and fertility can be preserved.
